absent_no_file.cause: never landed, deleted, partial checkout missing the path
absent_no_file.fix: restore the file (git checkout -- path) or remove it from the suite list
absent_no_file.message_today: ABSENT $s — named by this stage and not executable on disk (TRUE but uninformative: absence is the specific fact)

present_mode_dropped.cause: fresh clone on a filesystem without exec bits, partial checkout, copy tool dropping mode, chmod accident
present_mode_dropped.fix: chmod +x, or git checkout -- path (git tracks the +x bit, so checkout restores mode too)

conclusion: SPLIT WORTH IT — the conflation hides cause while the stage's job is to name what is wrong. Cheap (4 lines), no behavior change except message precision, same rc=1 both branches.
directory_edge: A directory at a suite path passes -x (search bit) and falls through to execution (exit 126 RED, confusing tail). Unobserved, out of scope; noted, not pursued.

proposed_messages.absent: ABSENT $s — named by this stage and not on disk; restore it (git checkout -- <path>) or remove it from the suite list
proposed_messages.unexecutable: UNEXECUTABLE $s — on disk but mode dropped; chmod +x <path> or git checkout -- <path> (mode is tracked) to restore

same_next_action_objection: Answered: git checkout -- <path> repairs BOTH (content and mode are both tracked), so the operator's first command converges. The split still earns its keep in diagnosis speed (absent = supply problem, unexecutable = mode problem) and in the FAKE_MISSING family: the current --selftest covers absence only; a mode-drop arm (chmod -x on a temp COPY driven via an env-overridden suite path — never the real scripts, per the SLB refusal precedent) would cover the second branch. Recommend adding it with the split; do not chmod real scripts to test this.
